title: Powers and roots of algebraic terms

steps.title: Open the square
steps.action: Make two identical factors of the complete term 3x.
steps.narration: The exponent two applies to both three and x.

steps.title: Multiply the two factors
steps.action: Three times three is nine; x times x is x squared.
steps.narration: The area of the three x by three x square is nine x squared.

worked_examples.misconception: Squaring x but leaving the coefficient at three.
worked_examples.repair: Draw two 3x sides; multiply coefficient by coefficient and x by x.

steps.title: Duplicate the signed factor
steps.action: Place two full negative 2a factors, including both parentheses.
steps.narration: The negative sign is inside the squared group.

steps.title: Resolve sign and factors
steps.action: Negative times negative is positive; two times two is four.
steps.narration: Multiplying the a factors gives a squared.

worked_examples.misconception: Keeping a negative sign after squaring the entire term.
worked_examples.repair: Use a two-sign grid before multiplying magnitudes.

steps.title: Open the cube
steps.action: Build three identical complete factors of 2y.
steps.narration: A cube uses three factors, not two.

steps.title: Multiply the first pair
steps.action: Two times two is four; y times y is y squared.
steps.narration: Keep the third 2y factor ready.

steps.title: Multiply the third factor
steps.action: Four times two is eight; y squared times y is y cubed.
steps.narration: The complete product is eight y cubed.

worked_examples.repair: Stack all three coefficient and variable factors.

steps.title: Show three signed factors
steps.action: The whole negative 3t term appears three times.
steps.narration: An odd number of negative factors produces a negative result.

steps.title: Pair two negatives
steps.action: The first pair makes positive nine t squared.
steps.narration: A third negative factor remains.

steps.title: Multiply the last negative
steps.action: Positive nine times negative three is negative twenty seven.
steps.narration: The three t factors make t cubed.

worked_examples.misconception: Assuming all powers erase the minus sign.
worked_examples.repair: Count negative factors: odd leaves negative.

steps.title: Mark exponent scope
steps.action: In the first expression the minus is inside both factors; in the second it is outside the square.
steps.narration: Parentheses decide whether the minus is squared.

steps.title: Resolve both paths
steps.action: The first two negatives multiply to positive; the outside minus remains on the second.
steps.narration: These expressions differ by a sign for nonzero x.

worked_examples.repair: Draw a boundary around the base before multiplying.

worked_examples.skill: Square a product with two letters

model.description: Square a product with two letters

steps.title: Duplicate every factor
steps.action: Both negative 2ab factors contain a and b.
steps.narration: The exponent reaches the coefficient and both letters.

steps.title: Resolve the coefficient and signs
steps.action: Negative two times negative two is positive four.
steps.narration: Keep both letter pairs visible.

steps.title: Group matching letters
steps.action: Two a factors give a squared; two b factors give b squared.
steps.narration: The result has two separate square powers.

worked_examples.misconception: Applying the square only to b.
worked_examples.repair: List the factor copies for both a and b.

steps.title: Write two copies
steps.action: Two complete 3x squared factors are multiplied.
steps.narration: An outer exponent counts copies of the entire base.

steps.title: Collect coefficient and x factors
steps.action: Three times three is nine and there are four x factors.
steps.narration: The inner two and outer two make four x factors.

steps.title: Write one power
steps.action: Four copies of x are x to the fourth.
steps.narration: The coefficient nine remains outside the variable power.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding the exponents 2+2 incorrectly to the coefficient too.
worked_examples.repair: Count variable factors, then handle coefficients separately.

steps.title: Pair the factors
steps.action: Twenty five is five times five; x squared is x times x.
steps.narration: Each matching pair contributes one factor outside the square root.

steps.title: Take the nonnegative root
steps.action: Choose positive five and nonnegative x.
steps.narration: The principal square root is nonnegative under the stated condition.

worked_examples.verify: At x=3: √(25·9)=15 and 5·3=15; x is nonnegative.
worked_examples.misconception: Assuming a square root returns both plus and minus.
worked_examples.repair: The principal √ symbol selects the nonnegative value.

steps.title: Find matched factors
steps.action: Three times three makes nine, while a times a makes a squared.
steps.narration: The coefficient contributes positive three.

steps.title: Respect principal-root sign
steps.action: The nonnegative number whose square is a squared is absolute a.
steps.narration: Use absolute a because a might be negative.

worked_examples.verify: At a=-2: √(9·4)=6 and 3|-2|=6; writing 3a would give -6.
worked_examples.misconception: Replacing √(a²) by a for negative a.
worked_examples.repair: Test a negative input and choose the nonnegative magnitude.

worked_examples.skill: Take a cube root with a negative

model.description: Take a cube root with a negative

steps.title: Build three equal factors
steps.action: Negative eight is three copies of negative two; m cubed is three m factors.
steps.narration: An odd root can take a negative input.

steps.title: Take one from each triple
steps.action: One negative two and one m leave the cube root.
steps.narration: Cubing negative two m reconstructs negative eight m cubed.

worked_examples.repair: A negative times negative times negative stays negative.

steps.title: Copy the fraction three times
steps.action: Both numerator and denominator occur in each full factor.
steps.narration: The cube applies to the whole fraction.

steps.title: Multiply top and bottom
steps.action: Three negative a factors make negative a cubed; three twos make eight.
steps.narration: An odd number of negatives remains negative.

steps.title: Reduce to one fraction
steps.action: Keep the negative numerator over positive eight.
steps.narration: The final quotient is negative a cubed over eight.

worked_examples.misconception: Cubing the numerator but leaving denominator as two.
worked_examples.repair: Make three complete fraction cards before multiplying.

worked_examples.q: A learner writes √(16x²) = 4x for every real x. Locate the error and repair it.
states: The first error is assuming √(x²)=x for negative x

steps.title: Test a negative input
steps.action: Substitute negative two in both the original and the learner claim.
steps.narration: The two values disagree, exposing the sign error.

steps.title: Locate the first invalid step
steps.action: Four is correct, but x is negative when x is negative.
steps.narration: The principal root cannot be negative.

steps.title: Repair with magnitude
steps.action: Replace x by absolute x so the answer is nonnegative.
steps.narration: The repaired rule works on either side of zero.

worked_examples.verify: At x=-2: original 8 and repaired 4|-2|=8; at x=2 both are 8.
worked_examples.misconception: Accepting a single positive test as a proof for every real input.
worked_examples.repair: Test both signs and restore the principal-root condition.

worked_examples.skill: Cube root of multiple factor groups

model.description: Cube root of multiple factor groups

steps.title: Group the triples
steps.action: Make three negative threes, three a factors and three b factors.
steps.narration: Each cube-root group has three matching factors.

steps.title: Take one factor from every triple
steps.action: One negative three, one a and one b remain.
steps.narration: An odd root does not need absolute-value bars.

worked_examples.misconception: Adding absolute bars to cube-root variables.
worked_examples.repair: Cube a negative test value to see the original sign is preserved.

steps.title: Square the first whole term
steps.action: Two x times two x makes four x squared.
steps.narration: The second x squared stays visible.

steps.title: Combine like powers
steps.action: Four x squared plus one x squared makes five x squared.
steps.narration: Both terms have the same variable power.

steps.title: Substitute the signed input
steps.action: Put negative three inside parentheses before squaring.
steps.narration: The square is positive nine, not negative nine.

steps.title: Multiply the coefficient
steps.action: Five multiplied by nine equals forty five.
steps.narration: The numerical value is forty five.

worked_examples.repair: Square complete bases, combine like terms, then substitute.

worked_examples.q: For x ≥ 0, simplify √(36x²) + ∛(-8x³), then evaluate at x=4.

steps.title: Pair square-root factors
steps.action: Six times six is thirty six and x times x is x squared.
steps.narration: Because x is nonnegative the principal square root is six x.

steps.title: Group cube-root triples
steps.action: Negative two cubed is negative eight, while x cubed gives x.
steps.narration: The cube root is negative two x.

steps.title: Collect like terms
steps.action: Six x minus two x equals four x.
steps.narration: Retain the original x at least zero condition.

steps.title: Evaluate the chosen input
steps.action: Four times four is sixteen.
steps.narration: This is the value at x equal to four.

worked_examples.misconception: Forgetting the negative cube-root term or the square-root condition.
worked_examples.repair: Place a sign and root badge on each independent branch.

practice_questions: Two negative factors make a positive.
Mark the scope of each minus.
Square the coefficient and both letters.
A learner claims √(25n²)=5n for every real n. Correct it.
At n=-1 the left is 5, not -5; correct form is 5|n|.
For x ≥ 0, simplify √(25x²)+∛(-x³), then evaluate at x=3.
Use separate square and cube-root branches.
mastery_questions: Simplify √(49x²) for any real x and check x=-2.
Three copies of -4, p and q give -4pq.
For x ≥ 0 simplify √(9x²)+∛(-8x³)+(2x)², then evaluate at x=2.
reassessment_questions: For x ≥ 0 simplify √(16x²)+∛(-27x³), then evaluate at x=5.
